skill.name: commit-drafter
skill.description: Automatically draft commit messages by analyzing git status and staged changes
skill.summary: Automatically draft commit messages by analyzing git status and staged changes
skill.author: abereyes

content.value_statement: Writing commit messages from staged changes takes time and can miss important context. This skill gathers Git status, staged diffs, and change statistics so Claude, Codex, or Claude Code can draft a review-ready message.
actual_capabilities: Runs local Git status checks to find staged files.
Collects staged diff statistics for changed files.
Prints full staged diff context for AI review.
Groups files by added, modified, deleted, and renamed status.
Provides instructions for summary and What, Why, How sections.
limitations: Requires a Git repository with staged changes.
Does not create commits or run git commit.
May expose staged diff content to the active AI session.
Does not verify issue trackers or project conventions automatically.

use_cases.title: Prepare Commit Messages
use_cases.description: Draft a clear message from staged changes before creating a commit.

use_cases.title: Summarize Review Work
use_cases.description: Turn a staged patch into a concise summary for pull request preparation.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Commits
use_cases.description: Help teams produce consistent commit summaries with structured change context.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a commit message for my staged changes and show it for review.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when you need a simple message from staged files.

prompt_templates.title: Structured Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a commit message with a summary line and What, Why, How sections for my staged changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when your project prefers structured commit descriptions.

prompt_templates.title: Conventional Style
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my staged changes and draft a conventional commit style message with a clear scope.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when your repository follows conventional commit practices.

prompt_templates.title: Review-Focused Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the staged diff, identify the main intent, and draft a concise commit message that avoids unrelated details.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the staged changes include several files or mixed updates.

output_examples.input: A developer staged changes that add form validation and update related tests.
output: What: Add validation checks and update test coverage.
Why: Prevent invalid form submissions from reaching the server.
How: Validate required fields before submission and cover failure cases.

output_examples.input: A reviewer staged documentation updates for a setup guide.
output: What: Clarify installation steps and environment requirements.
Why: Reduce onboarding mistakes for new contributors.
How: Rewrite setup instructions and add missing prerequisites.

output_examples.input: An engineering lead staged changes that rename a module and adjust imports.
output: What: Rename the module and update dependent imports.
Why: Align naming with current project terminology.
How: Apply the new name across affected source files.

best_practices: Stage only the files that belong in the same commit.
Review the generated message before committing.
Remove sensitive or unrelated staged changes before drafting.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as a replacement for reviewing the diff.
Do not stage secrets or private data before drafting.
Do not accept messages that misstate the purpose of the change.

faq.question: Does this skill create the commit automatically?
faq.answer: No. It drafts a message for review and does not run git commit.

faq.question: Does it require staged changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It reads staged Git changes, so files must be added to the staging area first.

faq.question: What information does it inspect?
faq.answer: It inspects Git status, staged diff statistics, and the full staged diff.

faq.question: Can it follow my team's commit format?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask for your preferred format, such as conventional commits or a specific section layout.

faq.question: Does it send data over the network?
faq.answer: The script itself does not make network requests. The active AI tool may process the diff in its normal session.

faq.question: Is it safe for private repositories?
faq.answer: Use care because staged diff content is shown to the AI session. Review staged files before running it.
